originalTitle: Congressman says TikTok backed out of a meeting to avoid child safety questions
summary: TikTok backed out of a congressional committee's "public roundtable" set for this month over concerns it would be asked about child safety practices, the chair of the committee said. After negotiating "in good faith" to bring TikTok's chief security officer before the House Select Committee on China to answer questions about Chinese government access to […]
content: TikTok backed out of a congressional committee’s “public roundtable” set for this month over concerns it would be asked about child safety practices, the chair of the committee said. After negotiating “in good faith” to bring TikTok’s chief security officer before the House Select Committee on China to answer questions about Chinese government access to Americans’ data and the TikTok algorithm, Chair John Moolenaar (R-MI) said in a statement Thursday that the company reversed course. “Now, TikTok is refusing to appear citing its own desire to avoid broader scrutiny of its child safety practices,” Moolenaar wrote. TikTok did not immediately respond to a request for comment. TikTok reneged on its commitment on August 27th, Moolenaar told Bloomberg in an interview — a day after Meta reached its sweeping settlement with state attorneys general and called on TikTok and YouTube to follow suit. All three of those tech platforms still have many pending suits focused on their child safety practices. “They claimed that in light of Meta’s settlement with state attorneys general, they wouldn’t be able to answer questions on child-safety issues,” Moolenaar told Bloomberg, even though he said the meeting was not set to focus on that topic.  Moolenaar said in his statement that the committee would attempt to reschedule. “We will continue to work in good faith to protect the American people and ensure TikTok executives publicly address the Committee’s questions regarding its operations and safeguards – consistent with the requirements of the Protecting Americans From Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act – before the end of the year.” The law Moolenaar references is the one that briefly banned TikTok from the US, before enforcement was repeatedly delayed by President Donald Trump. Ultimately, a deal to make its US service part of a new entity closed in January, theoretically resolving the security issues the law cited. But lawmakers on the Select Committee had lingering concerns even after that happened. In a statement after the deal closed, Moolenaar said TikTok would need to answer questions about Chinese government influence on the algorithm and US data protection to the committee directly.
chineseTitle: 国会议员称 TikTok 退出会议是为了避免儿童安全问题
chineseSummary: 国会委员会主席表示，TikTok 退出了本月举行的国会委员会“公开圆桌会议”，因为担心会被问及儿童安全做法。在“真诚地”谈判将 TikTok 的首席安全官带到众议院中国特别委员会，回答有关中国政府访问的问题之后 […]
chineseContent: 国会委员会主席表示，TikTok 退出了本月举行的国会委员会“公开圆桌会议”，因为担心会被问及儿童安全做法。在“真诚地”谈判让 TikTok 首席安全官出席众议院中国问题特别委员会，回答有关中国政府获取美国人数据和 TikTok 算法的问题后，主席约翰·穆勒纳尔 (R-MI) 在周四的一份声明中表示，该公司改变了方向。穆勒纳尔写道：“现在，TikTok 拒绝露面，理由是它希望避免对其儿童安全做法进行更广泛的审查。” TikTok 没有立即回应置评请求。 Moolenaar 在接受彭博社采访时表示，TikTok 在 8 月 27 日违背了承诺。一天前，Meta 与州总检察长达成了全面和解，并呼吁 TikTok 和 YouTube 效仿。这三个科技平台仍有许多针对其儿童安全做法的未决诉讼。穆勒纳尔告诉彭博社：“他们声称，鉴于梅塔与州总检察长达成的和解，他们将无法回答有关儿童安全问题的问题，”尽管他表示会议不会集中讨论该主题。  穆勒纳尔在声明中表示，委员会将尝试重新安排时间。 “我们将继续真诚地努力保护美国人民，并确保 TikTok 高管在年底前公开回应委员会关于其运营和保障措施的问题——符合《保护美国人免受外国对手控制应用程序侵害法案》的要求。” Moolenaar 引用的法律是在美国短暂禁止 TikTok 的法律，之后多纳尔总统一再推迟执行
